deviations.what: T004 (is_data_assessor/is_data_curator) was implemented and committed before T003 (states.py), reversing the brief's listed task order.
deviations.why: plan.md's own design states transition functions take 'the assessment and the acting person' and enforce the curator-only rule directly, so states.py must call is_data_curator. Writing T003 first would have meant either forward-declaring permissions.py inside the states task or writing states.py against a predicate that did not exist yet. Reordering two blocking Phase-1 tasks carries no scope or acceptance-criteria change to either.

deviations.what: T006's status->state mapping (OPEN->DESCRIBED, PENDING->AWAITING_DECISION, COMPLETE->COMPLETE) is a judgement call the brief and data-model.md do not specify numerically.
deviations.why: data-model.md says only that 'the existing status field is migrated into state rather than kept alongside'; it does not name the value mapping. OPEN ('not yet reviewed') maps most naturally to DESCRIBED ('not yet uploaded'), PENDING to AWAITING_DECISION, COMPLETE to COMPLETE. The review app has no tests and no wired-up upload path before this feature, so this table almost certainly migrates zero real rows; the mapping is recorded in a comment beside STATUS_TO_STATE in the migration and pinned by tests/test_review/test_migrations.py::TestStatusToStateMapping.

deviations.what: uploaded_by, decided_by are nullable FKs (null=True, blank=True, on_delete=SET_NULL), and Review's fields did not need an explicit reversibility/backfill migration step.
deviations.why: data-model.md does not state nullability for uploaded_by; adding a required FK via migration needs either a default or a guarantee of zero existing rows, and null=True is the safe, non-destructive default in the direction described in plan.md ('the safe outcome is the one that happens when nothing runs'). US-2's create view (out of scope here) always sets uploaded_by at creation, so nothing in this story's own tests exercises an unset uploaded_by outside test setup.

deviations.what: T009's per-row column headings are read from the importing resource's own field declarations (GHFDBParentImportResource.fields / GHFDBChildImportResource.fields, attribute->column_name), not from project/ghfdb/columns.py as tasks.md's prose names.
deviations.why: columns.py's PublishedColumns.ENTRIES covers only columns a published changelist displays and omits several input-only template columns this report also has to name (lat_NS, elevation, Country, Region, Continent, Domain, and every field-only column with no export accessor). It is therefore incomplete for this purpose and would produce empty or wrong headings for a majority of possible faults. The resource's own field declarations are the complete, authoritative attribute->column_name map already used identically elsewhere in this codebase (list_display construction). Documented in report.py's module docstring.

deviations.what: T010 required no production code change. The vocabulary failure path (ConceptWidget, MultiConceptWidget) already named the supplied value and the vocabulary in its raised message before this story began.
deviations.why: Confirmed by probe per craft-tdd: the widget message was temporarily reduced to a bare 'invalid value' string, the new test observed failing for exactly that reason, and the original code was restored byte-for-byte (git diff empty) before committing. The story lands as a report-layer test only.

deviations.what: T010a additionally deleted project/review/views.py, project/review/forms.py, project/review/utils.py, project/review/templates/cotton/review/card.html in full, and emptied project/review/urls.py and project/review/menus.py — well beyond the four view classes, two forms and two routes tasks.md names explicitly.
deviations.why: tasks.md's own acceptance criterion for T010a is a grep-verified absence of any reference to STATUS_CHOICES, review__status, or a Reviewers group anywhere in project/. ReviewListView (not in the named deletion list) used a ReviewFilterSet built on the retired lowercase 'reviewers' group and rendered current_user_is_reviewer from a 'Reviewers' group lookup; leaving it in place while deleting only the four named classes would have left ReviewListView referencing an undefined ReviewFilterSet (if that class alone were deleted) or left a live 'Reviewers' group reference (if it were not). Rewriting ReviewListView to use the new is_data_assessor/is_data_curator predicates was not an option: the brief's prohibitions explicitly forbid building or modifying user-facing views/forms/templates/URLs for US-1 through US-6. Deleting the whole superseded surface, leaving urls.py/menus.py as documented empty stubs for US-1 to fill in, is the only path that satisfies both the acceptance criterion and the prohibition. docs/data_models/ghfdb-erd.md was also updated (Review's new fields, a new SubmittedFile entity) because a pre-existing test, tests/test_docs/test_data_model_diagram.py::test_every_project_model_is_an_entity, fails otherwise — not itself a T010a task, but required to keep a pre-existing test green.

concerns: `poetry run python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (project-wide, no app filter) reports one pending migration for the third-party 'orbit' app, unrelated to review/ghfdb/heat_flow. Confirmed pre-existing on the verified base commit (a19283d2) before any of this story's changes, via git stash. Not touched — outside this story's scope and outside the three apps the repo's own tests/test_migrations.py checks.

Old dead-code cleanup went slightly beyond the brief's named list (see deviation 6) to satisfy the brief's own acceptance test; Forge should confirm this reading of D13 ('superseded views are deleted in the same phase that changes the record') against the phase, not just the task, is the intended scope.
